**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Rehash resolver decisions after canonicalization**

Whenever resolver outputs are finalized, this hash is calculated before `shared.load_outputs()` reconstructs `resolved_extraction` and canonicalizes structural field decisions. Consequently, every one of the 134 decisions published in `resolver-decision-ledger.v1.json` has a `provenance.record_sha256` that does not match the canonical decision with that field excluded, even though the nested extraction hashes are valid. Recompute the decision hash after all loader normalization so the published provenance can actually verify the artifact.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Verify resolver records against terminal manifests**

If any producer record is modified after the terminal receipts are written, this code accepts the changed set as long as the number of JSON files remains correct. `validate_producer_receipts()` verifies that the custody and validation receipts bind the producer manifest (including its `record_set_sha256` for shard 01), but the freshly computed hashes of `files` are never compared with that manifest before the decisions are normalized and published. This leaves the claimed terminal custody unable to detect altered resolver decisions; recompute and compare the producer record set against each terminal-manifest dialect rather than checking only `len(files)`.

The shared validator rejects that contradictory flag, but this override subsequently publishes `candidate_responses_used: false` in the import receipt regardless, so a contaminated checker lane can be certified as candidate-blind.
